Top candidates: Anthracnose (brown spots on stems/petioles), Cercospora (reddish-purple on stems/petioles), Phytophthora (dark stem discoloration), Diaporthe (pycnidia on stems).

**Test image summary:**
- Close-up of a soybean stem/petiole at what appears to be R5-R6 growth stage (green pods visible)
- Dark brown to reddish-brown discoloration running longitudinally along the outer stem surface
- Elongated lesion pattern; no white mold, no distinct circular spots
- Soybean trichomes (hairs) visible throughout

**Comparison against candidates:**
- **Diaporthe**: The reference image (bottom-left panel) showed an elongated brownish discoloration running along a green stem — closest visual match. Symptoms described at R6-R8, consistent with green pods visible. Pycnidia may not yet be clearly formed at this stage.
- **Anthracnose**: Reference showed darker, blacker irregular spots/lesions mainly on dry pods and stems; the test image has more of a reddish-brown tone, not jet-black acervuli.
- **Cercospora**: Reference was primarily leaf symptoms (purple/bronze discoloration); stem involvement is mentioned in description but the reference doesn't show it prominently.
- **Phytophthora**: Dark stem discoloration but from soil line upward on dying plants; test plant appears healthy with green pods.
- All root-rot diseases (Fusarium, Pythium, Rhizoctonia, Charcoal_Rot): Don't match — those affect lower stem/roots on dying/seedling plants.

The elongated brownish-reddish discoloration on a reproductive-stage stem with green pods most closely matches **Diaporthe (pod and stem blight)** as seen in its reference image.
